activity_summary: Anne kept the sword on the nail. Your father had spoken to the master: tomorrow morning is the leave, and the sword is not for school. You told Hamnet he is back at eleven. Judith put the ribbons under the same rule. You began to describe a cord, and Joan stopped you. Richard was already at the shop door.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Set today as the nail and eleven as the return, and took the cord back.

entities.name: Anne Shakespeare
entities.context: Refused the lane and the school, and sent them out after bread.

entities.name: John Shakespeare
entities.context: Gave tomorrow morning, and kept the sword out of the form.

entities.name: Joan Shakespeare
entities.context: Stopped the wooden sword, and stopped the description of the cord.

entities.name: Susanna Shakespeare
entities.context: Split the promise into the morning, the nail, and eleven.

entities.name: Hamnet Shakespeare
entities.context: Asked for the corner, left the bargain, and did not touch the nail.

entities.name: Judith Shakespeare
entities.context: Put the ribbons under the same rule, and kept hers.

entities.name: the lath sword
entities.context: Mentioned in The nail, and tomorrow morning

facets.activity: Kept the sword off the school lane

quotes.speaker: john_shakespeare
quotes.text: Tomorrow morning, and not the sword.
